name: West Point Lake
type: Stained Chattahoochee River lake; threadfin shad
pool: Full pool 635 ft; about 10 ft lower in winter

linesides.doing: Mostly 25 to 40 ft at creek mouths from Highland Marina to the dam and around Maple Creek, with sporadic surface schools. The downline bite holds all winter.
how: Popping cork rig, 3/8 to 1/2 oz white Rooster Tail or chrome C.C. Spoon.
Mid-depth crankbaits, Flash Mob Jr. A-rigs, big swimbaits.
Fish move above the 219 bridge; watch the shallow sandbars.

bass.doing: Coves and pockets with small feeder creeks, riprap and wood shallow; humps, drop-offs, brush and roadbeds at 20 to 30 ft. Low 60s water would turn on the shallow bite.
how: Jigs and shaky heads pitched to cover.
Jigging spoon or drop shot; spots in deep water.

crappie.doing: 15 to 20 ft, sometimes near the bottom, on bridge pilings, brush and blowdowns near old creek channels and deep docks in Yellowjacket, Wehadkee and Whitewater creeks.
how: Fish can move shallow enough to catch from the bank.

linesides.doing: Upper 50s is ideal. Fish drop-offs near the channel and hump tops at river bends and creek mouths: Yellowjacket, Wehadkee and Maple, and the lower lake. Ringer Access is a good place to start.
how: Cut shad chunked downstream on a short Carolina rig from an anchored boat.
Sassy Shads, bucktails, spoons, mid-depth crankbaits, Flash Mob rigs.
Gulls and loons find the schools.

bass.doing: Shallow wood, brush and riprap; ditches and creek runs that carry warm water; dark chunk rock, red clay and gravel banks in lower-lake creeks. Spotted bass begin bedding in March.
how: No. 7 crawfish Shad Rap, red squarebill, Rat-L-Trap.
Jig and pig or Carolina-rigged finesse worm.

crappie.doing: March is the top month for size and numbers. Blowdowns and brush in 3 to 6 ft on warm afternoons, trolling in 10 to 18 ft of clearer water, and bedding around the mid-March full moon.
how: Minnows or jigs under a float in the shallows.

linesides.doing: Many fish are up the rivers spawning while others feed on the main lake as the shad spawn begins.
how: Live shad or bucktails at bends and current breaks.
Topwater and flukes at first light on points.

bass.doing: Bass bed in pockets and creek backs around the full moon, on hard bottom near cover.
how: Swimbait or Fluke in the backs of pockets first thing.

crappie.doing: Crappie spawn in the backs of creeks in a few feet of water once it reaches about 62 to 65°F.
how: Float and jig or minnow in 1 to 6 ft.
Double jig rig longlined across the flats.

linesides.doing: Shad spawn on riprap, seawalls and points at first light, and linesides school on them. By June they move to humps and the main channel.
how: Topwater, flukes and small swimbaits around riprap and points.
Downlined shad or shiners on humps.
Small crankbaits and Swim Shads cast to surfacing fish.

bass.doing: Shad spawn on riprap and seawalls at dawn, then bass move to bream beds, docks and the first drop off the bank.
how: Spinnerbait, buzzbait or topwater on riprap and seawalls.
Shaky head skipped into the shade.

crappie.doing: Crappie leave the banks for docks and brush in 10 to 15 ft. Singles and small groups are often the bigger fish.
how: Minnows set just above the brush.

linesides.doing: Down-lake and on the main lake, where schools are surfacing.
how: Small crankbaits, topwater, popping cork rigs, Storm Swim Shad.

bass.doing: Largemouth on bream beds and riprap around bridges, then deeper brush and roadbeds. Spotted bass on sloping gravel banks.
how: Pop-R, Spook or buzzbait; cast a Senko where you missed a strike.
Best while the dam is generating.
Deep crankbait or Texas-rigged worm on brush and roadbeds.
Shaky head with a craw or worm, or a Carolina-rigged finesse worm.

crappie.doing: Deeper brush and structure after the spawn, and under docks. Night fishing is usually good in June.

linesides.doing: As the water cools, schools roam the main lake and creek mouths chasing shad. After turnover, a strong topwater bite usually follows.
how: Cast small swimbaits, spoons or popping corks into busting fish.
Shad on planer boards or freelines at sunup and sundown.

bass.doing: Shad push into creeks and pockets, and bass follow them shallow.
how: Crankbaits, spinnerbaits and topwater around bait in pockets.
Jig or shaky head on wood and docks.

crappie.doing: Crappie are on docks and brush early, then pull off cover into roaming schools in the creeks as the water cools.
how: Shoot jigs under docks with brush or shade.
Cast a jig just past a school and keep it above them.
Bright jigs in clear water, dark after rain.
